title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku Med Student. Tip #1
body: She's at ATU and she will tell you the year, not the degree, because the year is the whole personality. First year is anatomy and crying. Third year is when the confidence arrives and it is unearned. Sixth year is a person who has stopped explaining anything to anyone. Ask which year. Watch how fast the answer comes. It's a sealed deal if she can name the exact professor who failed her and the exact date.
caption:
Tip #1 😭 ATU students, I'm sorry.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku Med Student. Tip #2
body: Ask what happens after. Rezidentura, which is an exam everyone is afraid of, or the TUS in Turkey, which is the same fear in a second language. Half of Baku medicine is quietly preparing for Turkey and does not want their parents to know how seriously. If she has Turkish flashcards on her phone she has already decided. It's a sealed deal if she knows the TUS date this year without checking.
caption:
Tip #2 😭 ATU students, I'm sorry.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku Med Student. Tip #3
body: Watch the money conversation, because it's the wound. Six years, then residency, then a state salary that a twenty-three-year-old in IT clears in a month. Everyone knows. Nobody says it at the table with the parents. Mention dentistry and see what happens to her face, because dentists make money in year three and everyone in medicine has done that maths at 2am. It's a sealed deal if she has a cousin in IT and they no longer discuss salaries.
caption:
Tip #3 😭 ATU students, I'm sorry.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku Med Student. Tip #4
body: Ask where she wants to end up. Bona Dea, Liv, Mediclub, Baku Medical Plaza, that's the private tier and everyone names one of them. The state hospital is where she is actually working right now, for almost nothing, on nights, learning more than she will admit. Both things are true at once. It's a sealed deal if she can describe a shift that broke her and does it in a completely flat voice.
caption:
Tip #4 😭 ATU students, I'm sorry.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku Med Student. Tip #5
body: Look at the phone. Photos of a whiteboard, photos of a slide, photos of another student's notes, four thousand of them, none organised, all essential. There is a group chat where the entire year shares material and it has been running for six years and it is the only reason anyone graduates. It's a sealed deal if she has ever failed to find a photo she took specifically so she would not lose it.
caption:
Tip #5 😭 ATU students, I'm sorry.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku Med Student. Tip #6
body: Ask about the parents. In an Azerbaijani family a doctor in the house is a permanent status object, and she has been the answer to a relative's question since she was seventeen. Every wedding, every funeral, someone shows her a rash. She looks at it. She always looks at it. It's a sealed deal if a relative has described a symptom to her over the phone and then ignored the advice entirely.
caption:
Tip #6 😭 ATU students, I'm sorry.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku Med Student. Tip #7
body: Watch what she does with a free evening, because there are so few. Not Chinar, too expensive on that salary. A café near the university, one coffee, three hours, with the same four people who have seen her at her worst. Medical friendships in Baku are not friendships, they are a shared trauma with a WhatsApp group. It's a sealed deal if she'd take a call from any of them at 4am without checking who it was.
caption:
Tip #7 😭 ATU students, I'm sorry.
